title: Exact Weak-Null Inference for Binary Outcomes in Randomized Incomplete Block Designs
banked_reason: N-thin-survey: LuiChang2018 and LuiZhu2018 are directly relevant exact binary incomplete-block crossover papers, but only their abstracts were inspectable; theorem-level conditioning, target, and computational comparisons remain necessary for a supported field-level novelty judgment.
gap_reasons: N-thin-survey: LuiChang2018 and LuiZhu2018 are directly relevant exact binary incomplete-block crossover papers, but only their abstracts were inspectable; theorem-level conditioning, target, and computational comparisons remain necessary for a supported field-level novelty judgment.
proof_attempt_summary: Five proposal revisions developed and source-checked the fixed-menu finite-population optimizer, including full primary-text comparisons with Chiba (2017) and Lui--Chang (2015). The final reviewer found no soundness or structure defect and continued to rate the proposal at field tier, but would not certify novelty without theorem-level access to two closed 2018 predecessors. The run therefore stops before derivation as sound-but-novelty-unverified; a future re-raise should begin by obtaining those two full texts and comparing their conditioning laws and algorithms against the persisted proto-core.
tldr: Can exact binary weak-null inference remain computationally complete when incomplete-block treatment menus are themselves randomized with fixed global counts? The proposal asks this for the unit-weighted pairwise HT effect with fixed maximum block size and seeks to prove an exact projection to four response types and four menu-incidence classes, inclusive-tail coverage, and a histogram/flow/coefficient-convolution optimizer that returns worst-case p-values, labeled least-favourable completions, and exhaustive rational certificates. This would provide a finite-sample fallback precisely where the same-design asymptotic intervals can be fragile, while keeping unrestricted block sizes explicitly open and limiting novelty to the concretely specified fixed-menu coupling theorem and auditable outputs.
gap: Koo--Pashley define the fixed-count two-stage IBD law and asymptotic HT inference. Chiba (2017), PDF pp.3--6 and 9--11, is a verified exact stratified binary weak-null predecessor: it uses four response-type counts per fixed two-arm stratum, maximizes an inclusive one-sided tail over compatible nuisance vectors, and inverts tests into confidence endpoints by exhaustive enumeration. Lui--Chang (2015), PDF pp.2--5, instead studies six ordered two-period crossover sequences under a superpopulation random-effects logistic model, derives closed-form cell-count estimators and large-sample tests, and reports asymptotic Wald intervals rather than a compatible-table randomization optimizer. The unresolved mathematical object selected here is exact inference for the Koo--Pashley law in which a fixed multiset of multi-treatment menus is randomly placed across labeled blocks, creating global menu-count coupling. The proposed contribution is the four menu-incidence projection, labeled local/global compatibility, \([X^R]\) coefficient counting, fixed-\(B\) complexity theorem, witness recovery, and rational certification; broad priority over uninspected work is not claimed.
fill: The project seeks to establish, directly and audibly for that law, the four-by-four projection, exact coverage, integral compatibility flows, fixed-count coefficient counting, exhaustive fixed-\(B\) optimization, witness recovery, and rational verification, while legal counterexamples delimit aggregate summaries and monotone endpoint inversion.
